newsitem.title: THAILAND: Juldis denies cashflow problem rumours.
newsitem.headline: Juldis denies cashflow problem rumours.

text.p: Juldis Develop Plc on Monday denied stock market rumours that it was facing cashflow problems and said most of the company's funds were raised through the issuance of Euro convertible debentures.

"The company hasn't borrowed money from any foreign financial institution at all. Most of its funds were borrowed through the issue of Euro convertible debentures with a 10-year maturity period and the company still has seven years left to repay the $60 million amount of bonds," Terapot Charoonsri, the firm's chief executive officer told Reuters.
Juldis was ranked second on the list of most active stocks in terms of value and its shares were trading up 0.50 baht at 36.50 at 0511 GMT.

Terapot made the denial following last week's rumours that some property developer firms, including Juldis Develop, were having cashflow problems and may be unable to settle their debts with finance firms.
"Presently, Juldis Develop hasn't launched any new housing projects and it's now concentrating on projects that have been already completed," he said.
So far the company had sold about 70 percent of a total 170 units of low-rise condominiums on the northeastern mountain resort of Khao Yai, he added.
Another terrace townhouse project in the southern district of Hat Yai was doing well, he said.
